scimon.text: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

hidden_target.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr ink blend containing hydride powders (HfH2, NbH, TaH0.5, TiH2, ZrH2) and metallic Ti/Nb, dispersed in a polystyrene/binder matrix
hidden_target.intervention: 3D ink extrusion printing followed by de-binding in flowing hydrogen, and vacuum sintering at 1400°C for 18 hours with titanium sponge oxygen getter
hidden_target.conditions: Vacuum atmosphere (<3×10⁻⁶ torr), sequential heating to 1400°C, followed by water quenching from 1500°C for phase stabilization
hidden_target.structural_mediator: Sequential decomposition of hydrides driven by formation enthalpy differences (Ta→Nb→Hf/Ti/Zr), enabling in-situ alloying and oxygen scavenging
hidden_target.mechanism: Interstitial strengthening from controlled oxygen uptake (≈1.0 wt.%) combined with phase stabilization; quenching suppresses alpha-HCP formation to retain metastable beta-BCC; silicide coating provides oxidation resistance via self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 oxide filling
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Nearly fully dense bulk with metastable single beta-BCC phase (after quench) and excellent high-temperature compression strength; significant reduction in oxidation rate compared to uncoated baseline
hidden_target.baseline: Cast HfNbTaTiZr or uncoated sintered samples prone to cracking, alpha-HCP embrittlement, and rapid oxidation (k ≈ 570 mg² cm⁻⁴ h⁻¹)
hidden_target.boundary: Oxygen content must be maintained around 1.0 wt.%; cooling rate dictates phase stability (slow cooling yields alpha+beta, quenching yields single beta); sintering time must exceed 15 min to achieve full densification
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: In-situ X-ray diffraction monitoring of hydride decomposition onset temperatures and phase shifts during heating; post-quench XRD/EBSD for phase identification and grain size (target ~33 µm)
hidden_target.actual_result: Successfully printed and sintered alloys with ≈1 wt.% O showing excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures; quenching yielded metastable single beta-BCC phase with 33 ± 19 µm grain size; silicide coating reduced parabolic rate constant by ~700x (k ≈ 0.80 mg² cm⁻⁴ h⁻¹)
